_note: The research-return dock. A deep-research answer is a SECONDARY source: it licenses nothing on its own. This registry records the question that was asked, the answer that came back, and the routing decision for every finding inside it, so an answer either becomes governed content (via evidence_registry.json + evidence_annotations.json, per EVIDENCE_INBOX_RUNBOOK.md step 5) or a recorded decision not to use it. Nothing is allowed to stay undecided. Run: python3 bin/research-dock.py status | check | new. Runbook: docs/RESEARCH_RETURN_DOCK.md.

questions.title: What standards spine should govern the resident site?
questions.note: Asked twice on 2026-09-10. rq-1-2026-09-10 (chatgpt-deep-research) returned a crosswalk MECHANISM with a PLACEHOLDER framework and answered nothing. rq-1-2026-09-10-2 (claude) ANSWERS it: seven frameworks inventoried, Milestones 2.0 recommended as the resident spine on a VERIFIED express educational grant, a real crosswalk showing 43% unmappable, and a rotation-level 11/21 subset. findings.claim: The only COWS permission language located — "This version may be copied and used clinically" (Wesson & Ling 2003) — licenses clinical copying and does not on its face authorise public educational web display, so the 45 verbatim anchors are not covered.

primary.citation: Wesson DR, Ling W. The Clinical Opiate Withdrawal Scale (COWS). J Psychoactive Drugs. 2003;35(2):253-259.

findings.note: This is the direct answer to RQ-10 and it closes the interim waiver AGAINST keeping the anchors. Verify by retrieving the 2003 article itself and reading the template legend verbatim — the return quotes it via the PubMed abstract, which is secondary. If it holds, cows moves flagged-interim -> retired/restricted in instrument_rights.json with a new decisionRef, and the 45 anchors in withdrawal.html come out on the CIWA-Ar pattern. Blocked on f3: a withdrawal must leave a route. || CORROBORATED 2026-09-10: the NIDA-hosted form (https://nida.nih.gov/sites/default/files/ClinicalOpiateWithdrawalScale.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-10) carries the identical clinical-scoped permission line on an artifact independent of both the model and the paywalled article. That is a second witness to the LANGUAGE, not to the SCOPE analysis, so this stays needs-primary until the 2003 template legend is read directly. Note this finding's best evidence is a PDF with no DOI — the case that motivated the primary.url + retrievedAt + archivedCopy variant added in this change.

findings.claim: No scale-specific chain of title for the COWS instrument text could be established publicly; Taylor & Francis administers permissions for the journal article but is not shown to control the instrument wording.

primary.citation: Taylor & Francis permissions guidance for psychometric scales and questionnaires (publisher policy page).

findings.note: Practical consequence: a RightsLink purchase would not by itself clear the instrument. Any request must ask T&F to confirm it controls the COWS wording or name who does. Return estimates 6-8 weeks for a manual request, no published fee for nonprofit public-web educational reuse.

findings.claim: No current custodian-hosted canonical COWS form was found; the 2003 article's list of PDF hosts (ASAM, CSAM, UCLA ISAP, AlcoholMD) is historical, leaving the paywalled article DOI as the only defensible canonical link.
findings.note: FALSIFIED 2026-09-10 by direct retrieval, not by search. NIDA hosts a complete, current COWS form at https://nida.nih.gov/sites/default/files/ClinicalOpiateWithdrawalScale.pdf — all 11 items and severity anchors, source-attributed to Wesson & Ling 2003, carrying the same 'This version may be copied and used clinically' line. ASAM hosts a second copy (cows_induction_flow_sheet.pdf) but strips the copyright and permission line, so NIDA is the better citation. The claimed operational blocker does not exist: a retirement CAN leave a route and satisfy INV-IR2. The error is worse than a search miss — line 107 of the return names NIDA, ASAM and SAMHSA among the hosts it searched and dismisses them because the 2003 ARTICLE's host list is historical. It inherited staleness from a cited document and projected it onto the live web. Proposed failureMode vocabulary entry: source-date-contamination. One question remains and it is governance, not research: NIDA is a federal agency hosting a copy, not the rightsholder, so whether it satisfies the 'custodian URL, not a copy hosted here' wording of INV-IR2 is Josh's call.

findings.claim: The current PHQ Screeners site (Pfizer) states that no permission is required to reproduce, translate, display or distribute the PHQ and GAD-7 screeners, which is the express public-web permission WP-02c was left open to verify.

primary.citation: PHQ Screeners (Pfizer Inc.), current permission statement, select-screener page.

findings.note: Would move phq9-gad7 from provisional -> cleared. Verify by fetching the live page, not by trusting this quote, and archive a dated PDF/screenshot into the permissions file — the whole permission is a web sentence that can change without notice. Corroborated independently by the LOINC record for PHQ-9 and GAD-7.

findings.claim: The PHQ/GAD permission names reproduce, translate, display and distribute but not modify, adapt or create derivative works, while Pfizer's generic site terms restrict derivative works — so a faithful verbatim render is supported and an altered or restructured version is not.
findings.note: Sets the boundary for any programmed PHQ-9/GAD-7 form: unchanged wording, response options, ordering, time frame and instructions are inside the permission; changing any of them is not. Worth recording on the instrument entry even if the status stays provisional, because it is the constraint a future tool build would trip over.

findings.claim: No third-party reproduction licence for the BFCRS was found on the URMC resources page or in its training manual, and URMC is the scale's public custodian rather than an established rightsholder.
findings.note: Confirms the existing restricted status rather than changing it; the added detail is that manual searches for copyright/permission/reproduce/license returned nothing, so the current decisionRef's reliance on URMC site-wide Web Terms is the strongest basis available. Named permission route: Mark Oldham (URMC), with Andrew Francis, covering verbatim items, anchor ladders and any fillable implementation, and asking which entity actually holds title after the 1996 Munksgaard publication.

findings.claim: Official C-SSRS forms carry "(c) 2008 The Research Foundation for Mental Hygiene, Inc." and route reprints to Kelly Posner, so the project's free-use language covers use and not republication.

primary.citation: Columbia-Suicide Severity Rating Scale, official form copyright line and reprints contact (RFMH, 2008).

findings.note: Confirms the retired posture, but corrects a factual detail in the cssrs decisionRef, which records the scale as "copyrighted and licensed by the Columbia Lighthouse Project": the copyright holder printed on the forms is RFMH, with Columbia as the distributing project. If it verifies, that is a decisionRef wording fix, not a status change.

returns.question: RQ-1

findings.claim: The return does not answer RQ-1: frameworks[] holds one entry, EXAMPLE_FRAMEWORK, name 'PLACEHOLDER - replace with your actual standards framework', authority UNSET.
findings.note: Not a defect in the artifact, a scope miss. No framework was inventoried, none recommended, and all three entries[] carry _fixture:true. RQ-1's actual question — which of ACGME Milestones 2.0 / Program Requirements / ABPN blueprint / AAMC EPAs should be the spine, with versions, identifier schemes, unit counts and redistribution terms — is untouched. RQ-1 stays OPEN and must be re-asked. Keep the prompt as written; it was specific, and the tool answered a different question.

findings.claim: The zero-coverage rule family (V-20..V-26) enumerates seven distinct ways a crosswalk can claim coverage while delivering none, and is a stronger design than the single non-zero-exit check the agenda specified.
findings.note: The best thing in the return and the reason to keep it. The seven: no mappings; placeholder codes; duplicate padding; dangling codes; all mapped assets retired; all mappings merely tangential; and V-26 ZERO REACHABLE COVERAGE — mapped content that is scheduled in no rotation week. V-26 is the same defect shape as this repo's own hidden-not-indexed bug: content exists and is unreachable. Verified on receipt: the validator exits 1 on its own fixtures. Adopt the RULE FAMILY as a design input for check_standards_coverage.py; it needs no external primary source because it is a design idea, not a factual claim — promote when the spine exists to apply it to.

findings.claim: source_rights[] is a SECOND rights register that already contradicts instrument_rights.json on three of five entries.
findings.note: DO NOT IMPORT. instrument_rights.json is the single source of truth for instrument dispositions and is gated by instrument-rights-gate.mjs; a parallel register is the exact drift the decisions registry exists to prevent. The contradictions, checked 2026-09-10: (a) phq9 and gad7 marked redistribution_status 'verbatim_cleared' with rightsholder_established true and source_checked 2026-09-10 — but our register has phq9-gad7 as PROVISIONAL, phqscreeners.com blocks automated fetch (robots.txt), and RQ-10 finding f4 is still needs-primary awaiting a human visit plus a dated capture. The file asserts as cleared precisely what is unverified, and its own V-41 rule fires on it for a null evidence_snapshot_ref. (b) cows marked 'pending_permission' with rightsholder_established false — superseded hours earlier by decision cows-anchors-retired (PR #608): cows is RETIRED, waiver closed. (c) cssrs rightsholder_established true — RQ-10 f7 indicates the attribution is RFMH 2008 with Columbia as distributor, so 'established' overstates what is known. Same failure mode as RQ-10 f3: the model reasoned about our governance rules without reading our governance data.

findings.claim: The rights/text coupling rules (V-16..V-19) encode the de-expression principle independently: verbatim unit text may be stored only when the governing source is verbatim_cleared, otherwise the entry must use reference mode.
findings.note: Convergent design evidence, arrived at without knowledge of PR #608. V-17 blocks storing verbatim text against a non-cleared source; V-19 forces review.state to needs_rights_review when the source is pending. This is the same rule this project shipped today for COWS, expressed as a validator constraint. Worth citing in the proposed DE_EXPRESSION_PLAYBOOK as an independent restatement. Not promotable as a factual claim; it is a design convergence.

findings.claim: The validator requires the jsonschema package, which is not currently a repo dependency.
findings.note: Adoption cost, recorded so it is not rediscovered. Tier 1 is Draft 2020-12 via jsonschema; without it V-00 errors and Tier 2 is skipped. This repo's house style is stdlib-only for bin/ tools, so any adaptation should either add the dependency deliberately or reimplement Tier 1 against the existing validate_registry_schemas.py path, which already solves this problem here.

returns.note: Arrived as three files, not prose: a crosswalk registry, its schema, and a two-tier validator. Files preserved verbatim in rq-1-2026-09-10.files/ beside the return note. Zero invisible characters on intake.

returns.question: RQ-1

findings.claim: The ACGME Psychiatry Milestones carry an express third-party educational reproduction grant, which is the only affirmative grant in the whole inventory and is what makes verbatim subcompetency identifiers and titles publishable here.

primary.citation: ACGME Psychiatry Milestones, Second Revision March 2020, implementation 1 July 2021 — page copyright line.

findings.note: VERIFIED VERBATIM 2026-09-10 by direct fetch of the primary PDF, not a search snippet: '(c)2020 Accreditation Council for Graduate Medical Education (ACGME) All rights reserved except the copyright owners grant third parties the right to use the Psychiatry Milestones on a non-exclusive basis for educational purposes.' The return quoted it accurately. Dated capture stored at 13_Faculty_Resources/rights-captures/acgme-milestones-copyright-2026-09-10.txt. Stays needs-primary for a STRUCTURAL reason, not an evidential one: promotion to adopt requires landedIn, and nothing has landed — no spine is chosen and no page is mapped. The evidence is ready; the decision is Josh's.

findings.claim: Milestones 2.0 comprises 21 subcompetencies — PC1-6, MK1-4, SBP1-3, PBLI1-2, PROF1-3, ICS1-3 — with a stable identifier scheme suitable as a crosswalk key.

primary.citation: ACGME Psychiatry Milestones, Second Revision March 2020 — subcompetency tables.

findings.note: Identifiers and titles verified against the primary document; they match the return exactly. The COUNT was verified by summing the enumeration (6+4+3+2+3+3=21), NOT by trusting a reported total — the retrieval summariser stated 'Total Count: 24' while enumerating 21. Recorded because it is the same class of error the dock exists to catch: a confident number beside a correct list. Trust enumerations, not totals.

findings.claim: The ACGME Program Requirements carry NO third-party educational grant, only a bare copyright line — so the Milestones grant must not be assumed to extend to them.
findings.note: TREAT WITH SUSPICION — this is an unverified NEGATIVE, the exact shape that failed in RQ-10 f3 (the 'no custodian-hosted COWS form' claim, falsified in one fetch). The return states it did not locate a grant, which is honest, but absence of a grant in the PDF body is not absence of a grant: ACGME's site terms of use were not retrieved. This matters because the PR is the recommended SECONDARY axis and its clauses (4.11.f, 4.11.k) are the ones that would be quoted most. Verify before relying on it: fetch acgme.org terms of use, and include it in the permission email. Return's own Unresolved item 1 says the same.

findings.claim: The internal code `safety` collides with two different constructs — patient risk (suicide/violence, PC1) and institutional safety events (SBP1) — so mapping SBP1 to `safety` would manufacture false coverage.
findings.note: The most immediately actionable finding and it needs no external permission from anyone. Proposed fix: split into `safety-risk` and `safety-systems`. Note this interacts with a known constraint: FOCUS_CATEGORIES and SHELF_VOCAB are the SAME twelve codes, so splitting one touches both vocabularies and the shelf blueprint. Scope that before doing it.

findings.claim: 9 of 21 subcompetencies (43%) are unmappable to the twelve internal codes, and the pattern is not random — it is exactly SBP1-3, PBLI1-2, PROF3, ICS3, PC6 and MK4, because the internal codes are a disorder taxonomy and the Milestones are a competency taxonomy.
findings.note: The structural diagnosis, and it changes the remediation. Adding nine disorder-shaped codes does not fix a category mismatch; the return's recommendation is a second ORTHOGONAL axis (competency domain) so every page occupies a cell in a lattice rather than a slot in a list. That also distinguishes a real gap from a correctly-empty cell — e.g. PC6 Consultation x personality is legitimately empty because 4.11.k puts consultation on a different rotation. Directly relevant to the 61 undecided optional refs in check_path_coverage.py: a lattice cell reason is a better exemption reason than a sentence.

findings.claim: Both confirmed vocabulary gaps are worse than suspected: psychotherapy occupies TWO of 21 subcompetencies (PC4 and MK4) and is a hard Program Requirement, and QI/patient safety is SBP1 plus the 4.11.q administration requirement.
findings.note: Confirms the agenda's two suspicions and quantifies them. Feeds RQ-2 directly — the QI curriculum question now has a named subcompetency (SBP1: analyzes patient safety events / discloses them / participates in QI) and a named PR clause (4.11.q: utilization review, quality assurance, performance improvement) to discharge, rather than a generic obligation.

findings.claim: For the student site, LCME — not AAMC or ADMSEP — is the accreditor that actually binds clerkship objectives, and it was absent from the framework list entirely.
findings.note: A genuine scope gap in the QUESTION, surfaced by the return rather than asked for. If 'authoritativeness with accreditors' is a real criterion for the student site then neither candidate framework is what LCME holds the school to. This is the strongest argument for re-scoping RQ-1's student half rather than choosing between ADMSEP and Core EPAs at all. Also recorded: ADMSEP's Clinical Learning Objectives Guide is November 2007 and written to DSM-IV with five-axis and Somatoform/Dissociative topic areas — 19 years stale — while Core EPAs cannot discriminate psychiatric content because they are specialty-agnostic by design.

returns.note: Second RQ-1 return, different tool. This one ANSWERS the question: seven frameworks inventoried with versions and identifier schemes, a recommendation with stated trade-offs, a real crosswalk, a rotation-level subset, and a 13-item Unresolved section. Contrast rq-1-2026-09-10 (chatgpt-deep-research), which returned a placeholder crosswalk mechanism. Running one question on two tools separated a container from an answer — the habit paid on its first use.
